newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qantas frequent flyers yield big sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qantas frequent flyers yield big sales.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd said on Wednesday its frequent flyer programme costs the airline about A$10 million a year to run, but accounts for a A$1.00 billion in annual sales or around 13 percent of its 1995/96 revenue.
"Frequent flyer programmes are now absolutely critical to the revenue of airlines," Qantas chairman Gary Pemberton told shareholders at the airline's annual meeting.

"The programme we operate probably costs us about A$10 million a year to run, but it protects and ties in revenue that would come in substantially in excess of a A$1.0 billion a year," Pemberton said.
"So the significance of that is very important, and it is absolutely a critical part not only of our strategy but the strategy of our competitors," Pemberton said.
Pemberton said frequent flyer programmes are also a major part of the alliances between airlines around the world.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc and has a global alliance programme with the British carrier.
